transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Start time: 15:30 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Hale (Head of ML, Reynwood), Priya Patel (Platform Eng, Reynwood), Luca Moreno (Security, Reynwood), Janet Ko (Product, Reynwood), Evan Brooks (DevOps, Reynwood)
Shared artifacts: Redwood onboarding deck (link: https://app.redwood.ai/onboard/reynwood-deck), pilot-scope spreadsheet (link: https://drive.example/reynwood-pilot.xlsx)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on runbook, network and security prerequisites for Reynwood Logistics pilot. Discussed hosting modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), latency/cost expectations, canary rollout plan, and success metrics. Agreed next steps around runbook delivery, VPC info, and a short latency benchmark window.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Alicia Park (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and we'll kick right into the onboarding runbook. We have Marco and Priya from our side as well.
[00:00:15] Tom Hale (Reynwood): Hi, Tom here. Thanks. We're excited, we've been waiting to get the network bits sorted.
[00:00:20] Priya Patel (Reynwood): Priya here, I'll be owning the infra side.
[00:00:25] Luca Moreno (Reynwood): Luca, security.
[00:00:27] Janet Ko (Reynwood): Janet, product.
[00:00:30] Marco Chen (Redwood): And Marco here - I'll be your CSM, running the timeline.

[00:01:05] Alicia: Goal for today: align on pilot scope (throughput, peak QPS, SLOs), confirm security prerequisites (KMS, audit logs), and agree on an initial runbook deliverable timeline. Also surface any blockers.
[00:01:25] Tom: For the pilot we want to run a customer-support summarization flow, about 3k avg tokens per request, expect peak 8 QPS but sustained 2–3 QPS. Latency target is sub-400ms for p50 on the short path — but we can tolerate higher p95 during training windows. Cost is a concern, we don't want runaway token costs.
[00:01:50] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): Got it. For 3k tokens that's non-trivial — we'll recommend a dedicated instance profile if you want predictable tail latency, otherwise hosted with a quantized variant and prefix caching might work for cost. Also want to confirm sequences: are you using long-context models or are you chunking?
[00:02:10] Priya Patel: We'll be chunking and stitching. We do have a small KV cache in our service, but not persistent for inference cache.

[00:02:45] [00:03:00] Marco: Quick note — in our experience automatic prefix caching can drop per-token cost by 30-60% depending on overlap. We'll show sample batching configs in the runbook.

[00:04:12] Janet: A couple security questions — we require customer-managed keys in prod, retention of audit logs for a year, and enforce SSO via SAML. Can Redwood support an HSM-backed KMS and SSO federation?
[00:04:30] Alicia: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; hosted can also use customer-managed keys if you want. SSO/SAML & RBAC are supported at the org level. We'll attach the SOC2 and ISO packet.
[00:04:45] Luca: Are audit logs immutable?
[00:04:50] Priya Nair: We have append-only audit log storage and we can export to your SIEM. Small caveat: retention beyond 1 year may require enterprise add-on. I'll include that in the packet.

[00:06:00] [00:06:10] Tom: Network: we need to know IP ranges for VPC peering and expected egress. Also, if we do private deployment, what's the typical footprint on-prem?
[00:06:20] Priya Nair: For VPC peering we'll provide exact CIDR ranges; for private on-prem footprints it depends on model family and QPS. Roughly, a small dedicated cluster for 8 QPS at 3k tokens might be a 4x A100-equivalent ~= 4-GPU cluster with NVMe cache — but we should run a short benchmark. Note: I'm approximating here, and we'll size properly after a profiling run.
[00:06:50] Evan Brooks: Yup — we need a sizing number to justify purchase. If you can give a recommended config we can start budget approval.

[00:07:30] Marco: We'll run a sizing exercise in phase 1. The pilot plan in the spreadsheet suggests a 2-week smoke test followed by a 3-week load window.

[00:08:10] [00:08:35] Alicia: Success criteria proposal — p50 latency < 400ms for 3k token requests, p95 < 1.2s under 80% load, cost per request under $0.15 for the pilot workload, and zero P0 security findings. Thoughts?
[00:08:50] Tom: Those are reasonable targets. We may relax cost threshold depending on accuracy.

[00:09:30] Priya Patel: One operational ask — we'd like token-level cost reports and per-route latency breakdowns. Can we get that from the console?
[00:09:40] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token breakdowns and per-model dashboards. We can grant a view-only role to your finance and infra teams.

[00:10:05] [00:10:30] Luca: On the KMS side, we cannot export keys out of our control. HSM in customer VPC is mandatory. Does Redwood do bring-your-own-HSM workflows?
[00:10:40] Alicia: We do; for Private deployments it's straightforward. For hosted, we support envelope encryption with your KMS for key wrapping so plaintext key material never leaves your environment. I'll add the exact flow to the security packet.

[00:12:00] [00:12:20] Janet: What's the rollback story if a model rollout introduces regressions? We need canary and automatic fallback.
[00:12:28] Priya Nair: Redwood supports canary and percentage rollouts with automatic rollback on quality regressions defined by eval sets. You can bind prompt-based evals to a rollout policy; if quality drops below threshold we auto-failover to previous model variant. There was a small transcription glitch earlier in our docs where KV cache was written as KV "cash" in the doc — ignore that.

[00:13:05] Tom: Nice. For evaluation, we have a small held-out set — can we push that and run A/B in the platform?
[00:13:12] Priya Nair: Yep, we can wire your eval harness; we'll need a sample data export and we'll run both latency and quality metrics.

[00:14:00] [00:14:30] Marco: Admin and billing question: for Dedicated reserved capacity do you prefer annual commitments? We can do monthly reserved as well but price/perf improves with annual.
[00:14:40] Alicia: We'll include a cost estimate for monthly vs annual reserved and a hosted on-demand fallback.

[00:15:20] Evan: One tricky bit: our compliance team will want a data residency guarantee for EU customers. Do you have region pinning?
[00:15:30] Priya Nair: Yes, we can pin to regions and also do Private deployments in your VPC in target regions. We'll note the region option in the runbook.

[00:16:45] [00:17:00] Alicia: Ok, logistics — we'll deliver: 1) onboarding runbook and sample network diagram, 2) security packet (SOC2/ISO/KMS flow), 3) recommended cluster sizing + benchmark plan, 4) pilot timeline spreadsheet with milestones. Expect the docs by EOB 2027-02-05.

[00:17:30] Janet: Can we get a short technical deep-dive with the SEs for the model parallelism and kv cache behavior? Maybe 60 minutes?
[00:17:40] Priya Nair: Absolutely — I can run a deep dive next week. We'll cover attention kernel tradeoffs, continuous batching, kv cache eviction behavior (we sometimes see transcription errors where evict is written as e-vict, so watch the doc for typos).

[00:18:20] [00:18:45] Tom: Good. Also want to check: how do we instrument end-to-end tracing? We use OpenTelemetry.
[00:18:55] Marco: Redwood supports OpenTelemetry and we can inject trace hooks per-request; we'll add instrumentation examples to the runbook.

[00:20:00] Priya Patel: A couple of non-blockers — does Redwood offer generation quality monitoring and drift alerts?
[00:20:10] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Optimize can monitor quality via prompt sets and regression alerts tied to evals. We'll scope that as optional add-on for the pilot; include basic regression checks in the pilot plan by default.

[00:21:40] [00:22:00] Alicia: Timecheck — 30 minutes in. Any blockers we haven't surfaced?
[00:22:05] Luca: One: logging retention SLA — need to confirm cost for 13-month retention.
[00:22:12] Alicia: Noted, we'll call that out with pricing.

[00:23:00] [00:23:15] Evan: Also need a contact for SRE war room during the smoke test. I'll add Evan and a backup.
[00:23:20] Marco: Great — we'll have a Slack channel and an on-call rotation for the smoke test.

[00:24:00] [00:24:30] Alicia: Let's recap the pilot phases quickly: Phase 0: network/security setup and smoke tests (1 week). Phase 1: 2-week smoke + functional validation. Phase 2: 3-week load window for performance and cost validation. Phase 3: roll to prod on agreed capacity.
[00:25:05] Tom: Agree. Who signs off on production readiness?
[00:25:10] Marco: Typically the customer PM + Redwood CSM sign off; we'll formalize the checklist.

[00:26:00] [00:26:30] Janet: One more product ask — we want to evaluate structured output / function calling for our downstream processors. Is that supported?
[00:26:40] Priya Nair: Yes, supported. We'll include examples for structured JSON output and function/tool calling in the runbook.

[00:28:00] [00:28:15] Alicia: Timing: we'll schedule the SE deep-dive next Wednesday 2027-02-10 at 10am PT unless you prefer another time.
[00:28:25] Priya Patel: Sounds good for us.

[00:29:00] [00:29:30] Marco: I'll follow up with calendar invites and the pilot spreadsheet.

[00:30:10] Tom: One minor note — our legal team will want the data processing addendum; can you share a template?
[00:30:18] Alicia: Yes, we'll send the DPA and procurement checklist.

[00:31:00] [00:31:30] Luca: Also, can Redwood run a short red-team style security review? Not necessarily formal pen test but threat modeling for the integration.
[00:31:40] Priya Nair: We can do an architecture threat modeling session with our security SEs; I'll coordinate.

[00:33:00] [00:33:20] Alicia: Alright if no other open major blockers, we should wrap with next steps and owners.

[00:33:40] Marco: Recap of owners: Alicia -> runbook + network diagram; Priya Nair -> SE artifacts and benchmark plan; Marco -> pilot spreadsheet + Slack; Evan -> provide VPC and peering details; Luca -> KMS constraints; Tom/Janet -> signoff criteria and eval set.
[00:34:05] Tom: I'll get the eval set uploaded by Friday.
[00:34:10] Janet: We'll review signoff criteria internally and reply.

[00:35:00] [00:35:30] Alicia: Thanks everyone. We'll send the notes and action items. Expect docs by 2027-02-05 and the SE deep-dive invite for 2027-02-10.
[00:35:45] Priya Nair: Quick PSA — the sample sizing I mentioned is approximate; final numbers after profiling.

[00:36:20] Evan: Fine. Appreciate the clarity.
[00:36:30] Marco: One last thing — we'll set the primary success metric as the pilot p50 latency and cost per request; everything else is secondary.
[00:36:40] Tom: Works for us.

[00:37:00] [00:37:20] Closing pleasantries and short pauses.

End of transcript.
